source.title: A Systematic Investigation of Commonsense Understanding in Large Language Models
source.authors: Xiang Lorraine Li; Adhiguna Kuncoro; Jordan Hoffmann; Cyprien de Masson d'Autume; P. Blunsom; Aida Nematzadeh

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some text and tables show PDF extraction artifacts, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream commonsense benchmark accuracy across model sizes and extrapolates accuracy against log(parameter count); it does not measure pretraining loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The study does not test held-out cross-entropy loss power laws, small-run loss extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its relevant results are downstream accuracy across six model sizes and linear-regression estimates of model sizes needed for human-level accuracy. Answer-only baselines are included below as controls. Few-shot results and prompt/score-function comparisons are not extracted as rows because they do not test scale predictability.
record.test_reason: Measures zero-shot accuracy on four commonsense benchmarks across six Gopher sizes (44M–280B) and fits accuracy against log(params). This bears on V6 only. It reports no pretraining loss, token or compute scaling, allocation, shape or fitting-choice analysis.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find zero-shot accuracy consistently improves with size on all four benchmarks. They argue the gains are small on most tasks and partly reflect answer-only surface cues (HellaSwag, PIQA). Log-linear extrapolation implies 1.4T to over 10^18 parameters for human level. They also find results sensitive to evaluation choices (up to 19.7 points at 7B).
record.recipe_differences: The study measures downstream multiple-choice accuracy and fits accuracy against log(parameter count); it does not reproduce pretraining-loss scaling measurements or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Benchmark and evaluation design choices affect measured performance: prompt format, score function, scored span, and sentence conversion; the best-versus-worst setting gap is reported as 19.7 for HellaSwag, 16.2 for PIQA, 4.6 for Social IQa, and 2.3 for WinoGrande.

fits_no_version.finding: Answer-only accuracy, which ignores the question, also rises with size on HellaSwag (25.8 to 57.0) and PIQA (60.2 to 73.2). It stays near chance on WinoGrande and Social IQa.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Part of downstream accuracy gains with scale on multiple-choice benchmarks comes from exploiting answer-only surface cues.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The scaling sweep covers one model family, and the human-level parameter estimates are extrapolations beyond the measured range. The study evaluates only multiple-choice benchmarks. It also reports that answer-only baselines are strong on some benchmarks and that evaluation design choices cause sizeable performance differences.
record.rows_left_out: Few-shot accuracy rows and the prompt/score-function best-versus-worst comparisons were not included because they do not measure scale predictability. The paper reports these in Table 3, Figure 5, and Table 4; the knowledge-base augmentation results in Table 7 are also outside this version.

untested.parts: No loss extrapolation from small runs is tested.
No variation of shape at fixed parameter count.
Text-only, zero/few-shot evaluation; no other modality or training regime.
Predictability from pretraining loss; whether the accuracy fit predicts held-out larger models; model families other than Gopher.

missing.what: Zero-shot minus answer-only gap per model size. It grows with size on all four benchmarks, e.g. WinoGrande up to 20.28 and PIQA 1.19 to 7.29.
Few-shot (1, 10, 64 examples) accuracy per model size. Example: Social IQa FS(64) rises 40.9 to 57.5, a steeper scaling than zero-shot.
Social IQa zero-shot across 44M to 7B under a different evaluation setup (42.3 to 48.5), with knowledge-base augmentations giving no gain at any size.

record.verdict_notes: The record misread the garbled Table 3. Most HellaSwag, Social IQa and PIQA zero-shot rows took values from the answer-only column or the wrong benchmark; corrected values come from the Table 3 ZS column and Fig. 2. Corrected series are monotonic for all benchmarks. The 7B score-function and prompt sensitivity (Table 4) is at a single size, so it does not bear on scaling predictability. Model sizes in the text are 417M, 1.4B and 7.1B; Table 3 rounds them.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small training runs predict loss on much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and how each grows with training compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.

The study tests downstream accuracy versus parameter count on four commonsense benchmarks in the Gopher model family. It does not test predictability from pretraining loss, other model families, or downstream tasks beyond these benchmarks.
Dependence of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices and training setup.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot accuracy on HellaSwag, WinoGrande and PIQA, 44M to 280B Gopher models
relationships.reason: Corrected Table 3 values rise monotonically: HellaSwag 28.0 to 79.1, WinoGrande 51.3 to 71.1, PIQA 62.6 to 80.5 (r1-r12, r19-r24).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased monotonically from 28.0 to 79.1 on HellaSwag, 51.3 to 71.1 on WinoGrande, and 62.6 to 80.5 on PIQA.

relationships.reason: Accuracy rises monotonically but only from 42.0 to 50.2 over roughly four orders of magnitude in size (r13-r18). The authors' fit implies over 10^18 parameters to reach human level (r52).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy rises from 42.0 to 50.2 over roughly four orders of magnitude in model size, with the fitted trend requiring over 10^18 parameters for human-level performance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Zero-shot accuracy across the six tested Gopher-family sizes on the four benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that zero-shot performance consistently improves with size; the tabulated values rise overall, although Social IQa is not monotonic (r1-r24).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Answer-only controls across model sizes, especially HellaSwag and PIQA
reader_labels.reason: Accuracy without conditioning on the question also rises substantially with size, so some apparent downstream gains can reflect answer-only biases rather than reasoning over the input (r25-r48).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The large model-size estimates are extrapolations from the measured range, not validated runs at those sizes (r49-r52).
